records.name: Misiones
records.current_summary:
No Misiones-specific statute, enforcement series or incident pattern is documented for transgender visitors, and interior provinces without local reporting infrastructure generate few records even where risk is real — the silence reflects documentation, not demonstrated safety.

The documented picture is national and deteriorating: per a March 2026 Agencia Presentes report on the national hate-crime observatory's tally, at least 227 attacks motivated by sexual orientation or gender identity were recorded in 2025, up 62% year-on-year and the highest of the observatory's ten recorded years — one every 38 hours — predominantly by security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, beatings the main modality, in a context the observatory attributes to the national government's 'cultural battle' against LGBTI+ people; attacks continued into early 2026, including a life-endangering home invasion of an LGBTIQ+ organisation president in another northern province. An April 2025 Washington Blade feature describes the transgender community as facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' amid government policies; the underlying page is no longer retrievable.

sources.claim: Washington Blade (2025-04-10): Argentine trans activists told the Blade the community faces a 'chaotic, desperate' situation under President Milei, who eliminated the national Women/Gender/Diversity Ministry and dismissed trans hires made under the federal Trans Labor Quota Law (1% of public-sector posts), which activists say is no longer being implemented. Milei's Feb 5 2025 decree restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgeries and hormone treatments. The 2012 Gender Identity Law (legal gender change without medical intervention, 'X' DNI marker since 2021) remains formally in force but is no longer guaranteed, activists report.

Agencia Presentes (2026-03-19), national hate-crime observatory: at least 227 hate crimes against LGBT+ people in Argentina in 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, one every 38 hours, the worst of the observatory's ten years. Trans women and travestis were 62.5% of victims (142 of 227); 64.8% of cases (147) were physical violence against bodily integrity; perpetrators were predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, with beatings the main modality; the surge is attributed to the government's 'cultural battle' and hate discourse. The same period saw DNU 62/2025 restricting minors' gender-affirming treatments.

records.name: Neuquén
records.current_summary: The national dossier found no province-specific trans statute, enforcement series or incident pattern for Neuquén; it is listed among the units classified "no sub-national signal", with the explicit caveat that most such provinces retain contravención/faltas police powers — the instrument an NGO survey holds responsible for most arrests of trans and travesti people — so "no signal" here means "no documentation", not "no exposure". The February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law (minors' transition treatments; prison placement of trans detainees) apply to Neuquén as to all provinces, within a deteriorating national picture (a record 227 anti-LGBT hate crimes in 2025, up 62%).

records.name: Río Negro
records.current_summary: Río Negro legislated visibly on trans inclusion: a provincial statute reserves at least 1% of public-administration posts for travesti, transsexual and transgender people — one of only a handful of provinces with such a law, which signals a provincial official posture better than the national baseline, though the regional surveys found none of these quota laws was actually being complied with. In a country whose trans-death counts are small enough for one provincial case to be a real signal, the 2024 national MuMaLa registry lists a named travesti victim attributed to Río Negro (with La Pampa). As everywhere, the contravención/faltas police codes remain, and the February 2025 national decrees curtailing the Gender Identity Law (minors' transition treatments; prison placement of trans detainees) apply here too.
records.current_localsOnly: The 1% travesti/trans employment statute is a resident-only mechanism a visitor never uses; its visitor-facing value is the official-posture signal it carries (non-compliant as of the surveys reviewed).

sources.claim: Washington Blade (2025-04-10): Argentine trans activists told the Blade the community faces a 'chaotic, desperate' situation under President Milei, who eliminated the national Women/Gender/Diversity Ministry and dismissed trans hires made under the federal Trans Labor Quota Law (1% of public-sector posts), which activists say is no longer being implemented. Milei's Feb 5 2025 decree restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgeries and hormone treatments. The 2012 Gender Identity Law (legal gender change without medical intervention, 'X' DNI marker since 2021) remains formally in force but is no longer guaranteed, activists report.

Agencia Presentes (2025-02-06): Milei's government published DNU 62/2025 amending Article 11 of the 2012 Gender Identity Law to bar under-18s from gender-affirming surgical and hormonal interventions, and DNU 61/2025 altering prison-sentencing law to change placement of trans detainees. Legal experts and LGBT+ organisations call both decrees unconstitutional and say abruptly suspending adolescent treatments endangers trans youth; the decrees face judicial challenge. They apply nationally, to every province.

records.name: Santa Fe
records.current_summary: National sources: a record 2025 with at least 227 hate crimes on SOGI grounds (+62% year-on-year, one every 38 hours; security-force-perpetrator cases doubled, 17 to 64), the 2025 executive decrees amending the Gender Identity Law and prison housing (national, applies to every province), and trans activists' testimony on the resulting hostile climate. Against that frame this province is one of the few that measures its own exposure: the provincial government publishes violent-death statistics that include transfemicidios and travesticidios, Rosario hosts the Observatorio Mercedes Pagnutti monitoring gender violence, and national registers name Santa Fe transfemicide victims. No province-specific statute or enforcement series with a source was found.
